1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate line and letter spacing, though it is not a specifically dyslexia-optimised font.

2.why: Instructions are sentence case with no italics and only 1–3 line blocks; all-caps appears only in the codes themselves and the testing-only Logs panel, not in instructions.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centred card with large inputs and buttons that would reflow well on mobile, though the provided screenshots are desktop-width so mobile rendering is inferred.

4.why: Instructions are short and plain, e.g. 'Use the email for your new bank account', 'Check it is you', 'Keep these codes somewhere safe. Each code works once.'

5.why: Examples are shown for expected inputs: 'The code has 6 numbers, like 123456', placeholder '123456' in code fields, and placeholder 'ABCD-EFGH-IJKL' for backup codes.

6.why: No screen contains more than a few short lines of instructional text; nothing long must be read to proceed.

7.why: A 'Copy setup key' button is provided for the TOTP secret and a 'Copy all codes' button for the backup codes.

8.why: A scannable QR code is displayed on the authenticator setup screen as an alternative to manually entering the setup key.

9.why: Standard labelled email and password fields are shown, but there is no visible evidence (e.g. autocomplete attributes or manager prompts) confirming autofill or password manager support.

10.why: Every screen shows a 'Step X of 5' indicator at the top and one large high-contrast blue primary button (Continue, Send my code, Check code, etc.).

11.why: Each screen has a single primary blue action, but some screens also present several secondary buttons (Copy setup key, Hide key, Get a new practice code) alongside it.

12.why: Progress is confirmed step-by-step and completion is stated plainly ('MFA is ready… Setup complete'), though not every intermediate action (e.g. sending the email code) produces an explicit plain confirmation message.

13.why: 'Send a new code', 'Get a new practice code', 'Show my codes again', 'Show setup key again' and 'Hide key' are all offered, and the UI states 'Retries have no penalty.'

14.why: The observed error reads 'We could not sign you in. Check your email and password, then try again' — it states the problem and the fix without blaming the user.

15.why: The interface explicitly states 'There is no rush' and 'There is no time limit for reading or retries', and no countdown or timer appears on any screen.
